test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 22 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following best explains the liquefaction of gases under high pressure?

options.text: Higher pressure reduces the space between particles, leading to liquefaction
Increased molecular size leads to condensation
Gases expand indefinitely, so pressure has no effect
Higher pressure increases temperature, leading to phase change

solution:
The correct answer is __**Higher pressure reduces the space between particles, leading to liquefaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Liquefaction of gases** is the physical process by which a substance in the **gaseous state** is converted into the **liquid state**. This is typically achieved through the manipulation of **pressure** and **temperature**.
 
• According to the **Kinetic Molecular Theory**, the particles in a gas are separated by large distances and possess high **kinetic energy**, which allows them to move randomly. When **high pressure** is applied to a gas, the **intermolecular space** between the particles is significantly reduced. ***Hence, the primary explanation for liquefaction under pressure is the reduction of space between particles.***
 
• As the particles are forced closer together by external pressure, the **intermolecular forces of attraction** (such as **Van der Waals forces**) become strong enough to bind the particles together, causing the gas to condense into a **liquid**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **molecular size** of a substance does not change during this process; rather, it is the **void volume** or the "empty space" between the molecules that decreases. <st
